newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Striking Colombian truckers agree to resume talks.
newsitem.headline: Striking Colombian truckers agree to resume talks.

text.p: The head of Colombia's main truck drivers' union said talks with the government would resume Monday afternoon in a bid to end a nationwide strike that began at midnight Saturday.

"At this time the conditions are given for us to return to the bargaining table, and we'll do so at 3 p.m. (2000 GMT) this afternoon at the Transportation Ministry," said Javier Suarez, leader of the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC).

Suarez said a possible obstacle to the resumption of talks came Sunday when 21 strike leaders were "arbitrarily detained" in southwest Nario province, but he noted that the union officials had since been released and said the ACC was fully prepared to initiate a new round of negotiations with the government.
Transportation Ministry sources said the strike was only partly effective Sunday, with no more than about 30,000 of the country's 120,000 cargo vehicles staying off the nation's highways.

But Suarez, who spoke in an early morning interview with the Radionet news program, said all of the ACC's rank-and-file would join the work stoppage by midday Monday. The union claims to represent about 80 percent of Colombia's truck drivers.
The ACC called the current strike in March on grounds that the government, and private transportation companies, had violated terms of an accord that ended a strike last October.
